findings.detail: c-test-passes has no readable evidence that the named failing test now passes. The only related delivery is port report (artifact-6321a9bcb3508c7e) whose accepted goal was merely to run the suite and record a report, not that the named test passed; this package contains no report content (artifacts arrays are empty). Sub-acceptances marked c-test-passes PASS even on unrelated work (facts, diagnosis, patch), so those marks cannot stand in for a passing test result.

c-change-explained is not covered: no accepted output port delivers an explanation of the change. Existing deliveries are facts, diagnosis of the failure, a patch, and a test report. Diagnosis is not an explanation of the change; the patch is the change itself. No contribution goal_statement is to explain the change, and no explanation text is present in the package.

All four acceptances were recorded against requirements_revision 1–4 while the root goal is at requirements_revision 5, and every sub-review stamped both root criteria PASS regardless of that sub-goal. Combined with empty artifact payloads, the acceptances do not compose into verified root outcomes.

mission_criteria.reason: Accepted contributions show a recorded test-suite report and a patch, but not the report contents or any other evidence that the named failing test actually passes. Sub-review PASS tags on c-test-passes are not credible (applied to facts/diagnosis as well) and cannot substitute for a passing result.

No accepted artifact explains the change. Diagnosis records a failure analysis; patch applies a fix; facts and report do not explain the change. Judged as a whole, the delivered ports do not cover this criterion.
